text:
alice: Heads up — after deploying kernel-selector v2 to canary across regions we see a sharp drop in prefix cache hit in ap-sg1 and p99 tail spikes. Anyone else seeing this?

bob: Yep. Metrics: prefix_hit_rate ap-sg1 0.62 -> 0.44 since 2026-03-16T21:05Z. p99 went 280ms -> 560ms.

perf-bot: Profile digest: increased KV cache misses; cache_key generation time +2.3ms median on miss path; more unique key variants in ap-sg1 vs eu-us.

carol: Did the kernel-selector change touch key canonicalization? My quick read of the patch shows a micro-opt that moved normalization into the kernel thread and trimmed trailing newlines.

dave: I ran a quick trace. Hashes for identical prompts differ across regions. Old path used unicode NFC + collapse-trailing-newline; new path strips newlines and does NFKC. That explains the extra variants.

alice: Minimal repro I ran locally (pseudo):
```
# emulate normalize mismatch
from runtime.cache import normalize
print(normalize('Hello
'))
print(normalize('Hello'))
```
If normalize differs, same visible prompt produces different cache_key.

eve: Also worth noting: batching heuristics were changed in the same deploy. We now compute a cache_key from raw prompt bytes for batching speed — that bypasses the canonicalize step on some codepaths. So two orthogonal changes likely combined to regress hit rate.

carol: I'm drafting a PR to revert the batching key calc and reintroduce canonicalize in the kernel path + unit tests with multi-region fixtures: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987

alice: Immediate mitigation proposals: 1) Route ap-sg1 traffic to eu-warm for 30m, 2) run a prefix-priming job against ap-sg1 to rehydrate local caches, 3) block re-roll of kernel-selector in ap until normalized keys validated. Thoughts?

bob: +1. I'll create a routing rule and kick off priming job. Priming command:```
./tools/prime-prefixes --region ap-sg1 --workloads top100 --concurrency 8
```
Starting now.

dave: We should also add a diagnostic that logs canonicalization version/tag into trace metadata so we can cross-check hashed keys across regions.

carol: I'll own the rollback for the canary and the patch. Will open a rollback PR to revert kernel-selector for ap canary (PR 990).

perf-bot: Alert: routing change applied. Monitoring heuristics suppressed for 15m while priming runs.

alice: SLO impact summary: p99 target <350ms. current ap-sg1 p99 560ms. Need to restore below 350ms.

eve: I'll add a regression test in the perf harness that simulates prompt normalization differences across locales and compares computed cache_key equality.

carol: Plan and ETA: 1) rollback ap canary (owner carol) — 1h, 2) patch normalize + unit tests (4h), 3) run prefix-priming job (1h), 4) re-roll canary with extra checks and monitor (ongoing), 5) postmortem doc.

bob: Assigning owners: rollback @carol, routing/priming @bob, tests @eve, monitoring dashboards @dave.

alice: Thanks. Keep this thread updated with PRs and job ids.

bob: routing rule created, priming job started (job id: 20260316-57). Will update when priming reaches 80% of top100 prefixes.

carol: I've opened rollback PR 990 and canonicalize patch PR 987. Running local multi-region unit tests now.

perf-bot: After routing/priming, prefix_hit_rate in ap-sg1 improved to ~0.59 and p99 moved down to 320ms (monitoring window 5m). Continuing to monitor for regressions. :rocket:

alice: Great progress. We'll keep the canary rolled back until the canonicalize test matrix is green.

carol: Will follow up with a short postmortem and checklist to avoid keying divergences when we change batching/kernel codepaths.

alice: end of thread for now — please ping if anything changes.
